sentences.text: Imagine you're a sailor in the eighteen hundreds, and every lighthouse on the coast looks exactly the same.
By day, a tall white tower looks like every other tall white tower.
Steer toward the wrong one, and your trip could end on the rocks.
You see, lighthouses have a secret identity.
By day, each one wears its own paint.
In North Carolina, Cape Hatteras wears a black and white spiral, while nearby Cape Lookout wears giant diamonds.
But at night, paint is useless, so every lighthouse blinks to its own rhythm.
Cape Lookout, for example, flashes every fifteen seconds.
It's like recognising a friend by their outfit in the day, and by their laugh in the dark.
So the sailor checks the stripes, counts the flashes, and finally knows the way home.
All thanks to a lighthouse that got dressed up.
